title: QSAR Accelerated Discovery of Potent Ice Recrystallization Inhibitors
study_design: QSAR classification and prospective synthesis with cell-free ice recrystallization assays.

experiments.model: aryl-alditol chemical series; cell-free splat assay
experiments.comparator: PBS grain-size reference; model classification threshold of 70% mean grain size
experiments.outcome_name: Prospective precision among predicted-active synthesized compounds
experiments.result: Nine of 11 synthesized predicted-active compounds met the assay activity cutoff (82% precision). The calibration dataset contained 124 compounds with an 84/40 train/test division. This measures chemical ice activity, not post-thaw cell survival.
experiments.sample_size: 11 predicted-active synthesized compounds; these are compounds, not biological replicates

main_finding: A structure model enriched for prospective IRI hits within related chemical series.
limitations: No cell preservation endpoint in this study.
A chemical-series split and threshold selection can give optimistic estimates of performance on unrelated scaffolds.
Paper-local compound numbers require separate structure curation.
mechanism_claim: IRI was measured directly; cytoprotection and cell-death pathway inhibition were not established.
reviewer: root; selected source results and protocol details checked against archived XML

title: Small-Molecule Ice Recrystallization Inhibitors Improve the Post-Thaw Function of Hematopoietic Stem and Progenitor Cells
cell_types: umbilical cord blood hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells
study_design: Controlled cryopreservation of cord-blood leukocyte concentrates with small-molecule IRIs, viability and progenitor assays.

experiments.intervention: IRI 2 or 6 added to conventional DMSO formulation
experiments.timepoint: 5-week stromal coculture followed by 2-week colony assay
experiments.result: IRI-supplemented samples produced up to a 2.25-fold LTC-IC yield relative to DMSO control. LTC-IC frequency increased up to twofold; compound 2 frequency comparison p<0.05, compound 6 p>0.05. Formulation entries for compounds 2 and 6 describe alternative arms, not a combined formulation.
experiments.sample_size: 2 cord-blood units; limiting-dilution doses had 4–9 replicate wells
experiments.evidence_excerpt: resulting in a 2.25-fold increase in LTC-IC yields versus control

experiments.result: IRI supplementation did not rescue viability at 0% or 2% DMSO; there was no improvement at 5% or 10% DMSO and some conditions reduced viability. Functional progenitor benefits at 10% DMSO therefore do not establish replacement of DMSO.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: there is no increase in the CD34+ cell viability

main_finding: Some IRIs improved progenitor function at conventional DMSO concentration, while viability and reduced-DMSO results were less favorable.
limitations: LTC-IC experiment involved only two cord-blood units.
Human hematopoietic cells are transfer evidence for iPSCs.
IRI dose entries in the functional summary represent separate treatment arms.
mechanism_claim: Measured IRI and progenitor outcomes support physical-protection utility; they do not prove direct inhibition of a cellular death pathway.
reviewer: root; selected source results and protocol details checked against archived XML

title: Small molecule ice recrystallization inhibitors mitigate red blood cell lysis during freezing, transient warming and thawing
study_design: Hemolysis experiments under controlled freezing and repeated transient warming.

experiments.intervention: 30 mM compound 4 with 15% glycerol during repeated thermal excursions
experiments.cooling: Rapid dump-freeze to −80 °C, followed by repeated warming to −20 °C and refreezing to −80 °C
experiments.warming: Final thaw after 1, 3, or 5 excursion cycles; final thaw conditions not transcribed
experiments.storage: −80 °C between excursions; long-term duration not established by this summary
experiments.outcome_name: Intact RBC percentage after repeated transient warming
experiments.timepoint: After final thaw following specified number of thermal cycles
experiments.result: After three cycles, compound 4 gave 92% intact RBCs versus 55% with 15% glycerol alone; after five cycles it retained approximately 90% versus 36% with glycerol alone. These are integrity endpoints, not oxygen-delivery or transfusion performance.

main_finding: A small-molecule IRI reduced RBC lysis during repeated warming in a reduced-glycerol formulation.
limitations: Nonnucleated RBC findings cannot establish iPSC recovery or cell-death pathway inhibition.
Compound identity remains paper-local pending structure verification.
Thermal-excursion resistance is distinct from validated long-term shelf life.
mechanism_claim: Cell-free IRI and transient-warming results support an ice-recrystallization mechanism; no direct biological target is established.
reviewer: root; selected source results and protocol details checked against archived XML

title: Small Molecule Ice Recrystallization Inhibitors Enable Freezing of Human Red Blood Cells with Reduced Glycerol Concentrations
study_design: Graded slow cooling followed by dry-ice or liquid-nitrogen transfer; hemolysis assessment.

experiments.comparator: 15% glycerol alone under the same cooling sequence
experiments.cooling: 1 °C/min to −5 °C or −40 °C, then immersion in dry ice at −80 °C
experiments.timepoint: Post-thaw; precise measurement interval not transcribed
experiments.result: For transfer from −5 °C to dry ice, integrity was 84% with β-PMP-Glc versus 67% with glycerol alone. For transfer from −40 °C, integrity was 49% versus 25%. Thus efficacy depends on the cooling sequence.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: 49% with β-PMP-Glc versus 25% for 15% glycerol alone

main_finding: An IRI supported reduced-glycerol RBC preservation under particular cooling conditions.
limitations: High millimolar additive concentration and RBC integrity endpoint limit transfer to nucleated cells.
The paper also reports unfavorable doses/protocols; benefit is not universal.
Long-term functional performance was not established by this selected experiment.
mechanism_claim: Direct ice-recrystallization activity accompanies improved RBC integrity; direct inhibition of death pathways was not tested.
reviewer: root; selected source results and protocol details checked against archived XML

title: Small-molecule fulvic acid with strong hydration ability for non-vitreous cellular cryopreservation
study_design: Fulvic-acid fractions characterized in physical assays and sheep RBC cryopreservation.

experiments.intervention: 240 mg/mL crude fulvic acid in PBS
experiments.comparator: PBS blank and commercial hydroxyethyl starch concentration series
experiments.warming: 4 °C refrigerator for 150 min or 45 °C water bath for 1 min
experiments.outcome_name: RBC recovery after slow or fast thaw
experiments.timepoint: Immediate post-thaw; separate follow-up assessed stability to 24 h
experiments.result: At 240 mg/mL, recovery was approximately 45% after 4 °C thaw and 80% after 45 °C thaw. Best HES recovery for 4 °C thaw was approximately 13% at 215 mg/mL. Fractions differed in performance; this is not evidence for a single chemically defined molecule.
experiments.sample_size: Each test condition repeated in three different batches with test and control groups included
experiments.evidence_excerpt: around 45% at 4°C thawing condition and 80% at 45°C thawing condition

main_finding: A heterogeneous fulvic-acid material protected sheep RBCs without added permeating CPA in a short-storage experiment.
limitations: Fulvic acid is a mixture with origin-dependent composition, not an identified drug-like molecule.
High mass concentration; no direct human iPSC evidence.
Immediate membrane integrity and 24 h RBC follow-up do not establish long-term cell function.
mechanism_claim: Ice growth/recrystallization and hydration were studied; the results do not establish specific cell-death pathway inhibition.
reviewer: root; selected source results and protocol details checked against archived XML

title: Ice Recrystallization Inhibition Is Insufficient to Explain Cryopreservation Abilities of Antifreeze Proteins
study_design: Natural and modified antifreeze proteins compared by RBC recovery, ice activity, and model-membrane interactions.

experiments.intervention: AFGP1–5-ipp variant in HES cryostorage medium
experiments.comparator: Native AFGP1–5 in HES; other AF(G)Ps
experiments.outcome_name: RBC recovery and relationship to IRI
experiments.result: The modified variant promoted approximately 55% RBC recovery compared with 24% for native AFGP, despite reduced IRI and thermal-hysteresis activity. Other protein classes with different IRI activities had similar recovery. Model-membrane experiments showed stronger interactions for the modified variant.

main_finding: Ice-recrystallization potency alone did not predict RBC recovery; membrane interactions were an additional candidate determinant.
limitations: Protein/mixture results do not establish a small molecule with dual physical and anti-apoptotic action.
Mechanistic membrane models are simpler than living cells.
Doses, full thermal protocol and replicate hierarchy need further arm-level curation.
mechanism_claim: IRI and membrane interactions were measured; enhanced membrane stabilization is a proposed contributor, not proof of a specific death-pathway target.
reviewer: root; selected source results and protocol details checked against archived XML

title: The ice recrystallization inhibitor polyvinyl alcohol does not improve platelet cryopreservation
study_design: Paired platelet concentrates cryopreserved with DMSO alone or with PVA; recovery and functional assays.

experiments.warming: 37 °C for 8 min, then resuspension in prewarmed ABO-matched plasma
experiments.result: Recovery was 73.9% ±7.9 with PVA and 70.4% ±10.5 without PVA (p=0.61), providing no demonstrated recovery benefit in this small paired comparison.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: not significantly different from the control

experiments.outcome_name: TRAP6-induced PAC-1 binding and ristocetin agglutination
experiments.result: PAC-1 binding fell from 89% ±5% before freezing to 32% ±1% without PVA and 29% ±4% with PVA. Agglutination was also impaired without a significant PVA benefit.

main_finding: PVA did not improve platelet recovery or function at the reported dose.
limitations: Small paired sample; null result is not evidence of equivalence or absence of benefit in other cells.
Higher doses described as unsuccessful had no displayed data and were not extracted.
mechanism_claim: PVA's IRI property motivates the test; this experiment shows no functional benefit and does not identify the dominant injury mechanism.
reviewer: root; selected source results and protocol details checked against archived XML

title: Chemically Induced Extracellular Ice Nucleation Reduces Intracellular Ice Formation Enabling 2D and 3D Cellular Cryopreservation
study_design: Soluble pollen-washing-water nucleator compared with DMSO alone in suspension, monolayers, spheroids and cryomicroscopy.
interventions: pollen washing water (PWW), polysaccharide-based ice nucleator

formulation.compound: pollen washing water; active polysaccharide not fully characterized

experiments.outcome_name: Fraction of cells undergoing intracellular ice formation
experiments.result: Typically 40–50% of cells formed intracellular ice without controlled nucleation, reduced to below 10% with the extracellular nucleator.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: reduced this to below 10% of cells

experiments.intervention: PWW added to DMSO freezing formulation
experiments.cooling: In 96-well plates to −80 °C; exact ramp not transcribed
experiments.outcome_name: ATP content relative to nonfrozen spheroids
experiments.result: Controlled extracellular nucleation improved spheroid ATP-based viability. The assay includes post-thaw growth and can exceed 100%; it is not an absolute count of surviving cells. Monolayer effects were larger and more consistent than suspension effects.
experiments.sample_size: 4000 or 8000 cells per spheroid; these are starting sizes, not replicate counts
experiments.source_locator: Results Figure 3 and preceding spheroid assay description

main_finding: Controlling extracellular nucleation reduced intracellular ice and improved preservation of models with extensive cell contacts.
limitations: PWW's active material is not fully chemically characterized.
Cancer cell lines and spheroids are transfer models for iPSC applications.
ATP/resazurin endpoints include metabolism and growth; they do not establish lineage-specific function.
mechanism_claim: Intracellular ice reduction was measured directly; lower oxidative stress may follow reduced injury and does not establish a direct stress-pathway inhibitor.
reviewer: root; selected source results and protocol details checked against archived XML
